history: Qufu is the hometown of Confucius — the 'Holy City of the East'. The Temple, Mansion and Cemetery of Confucius (the 'Three Kong') joined the World Heritage List in 1994; the Dacheng Hall ranks with the Forbidden City's Hall of Supreme Harmony among the three great eastern halls. The Confucius ceremony has run for 2,000+ years; Confucian learning went from here across East Asia.
importance: Hometown of Confucius · Holy City of the East
foods: 'Never tire of fine food, never tire of fine mince' — ancestor of official mansion cuisine.
Coarse-grain wraps rolled with scallions — pure Shandong.
Confucius smoked tofu with woody smoke aroma.
Slow-steamed until the meat falls off the bone.
Ginkgo sweet dish of the Confucius mansion.
One duck, one pigeon — a famous dish with a story.
One of Qufu's three treasures — Han stele rubbings.
Boxwood carvings of the Sage's household craft.
scenes: The World Heritage core where Confucius is honored.
'First family under heaven' — the Duke Yansheng's mansion.
The 72-meter Confucius statue and the Great Learning Hall.
Temple of Duke Zhou beside the ancient Lu city.
Shrine of Yan Hui, the Master's favorite student.
Where Kong Shangren lived seclusion and wrote 'The Peach Blossom Fan'.
An experience park of rites, music, archery, chariots, letters and numbers.
